counterexample.explanation: reset no longer calls _advanceToNextDown, so the first getNext always returns the start tick, initialized or not. Tick 150 is not initialized. With start 150 and end 120 the walk returns [150] where it should return nothing. The liquidity result stays right only because an uninitialized tick has zero net liquidity.

summary: The repair removes the call to _advanceToNextDown from reset and leaves currentTick at startTick. The start tick is now always returned first, even when it is not initialized or not a multiple of the spacing. The extra tick has zero net liquidity and its reward-growth slot is not used by any existing position, so I found no new High or Medium flaw.
